captions.instagram:
How does a tsunami happen?

A tsunami is not a big wave from the wind and it has nothing to do with the tide. The sea floor jumps, the whole ocean moves, and a low, fast wave crosses it at the speed of a jet. Break the fault yourself, follow the 2004 wave across the Indian Ocean, watch it grow at the shore, and learn the three signs that mean go to high ground.

→ A tsunami starts on the sea floor. Two plates stick, and the upper one bends for centuries.
→ Then it snaps up in a giant earthquake and lifts the whole sea above it.
→ A wind wave only stirs the top of the sea. Deep down, the water is still.
→ A tsunami moves the whole ocean, top to bottom, at √(g × h): over 700 km/h.
→ 26 December 2004. The wave reached Aceh in minutes, India and Sri Lanka in about two hours.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/tsunamiclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a tsunami happen? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A tsunami is not a big wave from the wind and it has nothing to do with the tide. The sea floor jumps, the whole ocean moves, and a low, fast wave crosses it at the speed of a jet. Break the fault yourself, follow the 2004 wave across the Indian Ocean, watch it grow at the shore, and learn the three signs that mean go to high ground.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/tsunamiclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/tsunamiclear

In this video:
• The sea floor moves. Off Sumatra one plate slides under another at a few centimetres a year.
• A wave that moves the whole ocean. A wind wave stirs only the top of the sea.
• Across the ocean in hours. On 26 December 2004 the wave reached Aceh and the Nicobar Islands within about 15 to 30 minutes, Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu after about 2 hours (2 h 36 min at Chennai's tide gauge) and Somalia after about 7 hours.
• It grows at the shore. In shallow water the wave slows and bunches up.
• Warning systems. Earthquake waves travel about 40 times faster than the tsunami.
• 2004, and what to do. About 2.3 lakh people died in 14 countries, more than 10,000 of them in India.
